thread.title: Nvidia (NVDA) 4th Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Nvidia (NVDA) 4th Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Nvidia earnings (Shutterstock photo)
Will too much cryptocurrency exposure trip up Nvidia ( NVDA )?
The semiconductor giant is scheduled to report fourth quarter fiscal 2017 earnings results after Thursday’s closing bell. In the wake of the recent market selloff, Nvidia shares have gotten punished, falling some 18% from its January high, which significantly more than other tech heavyweights such as Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Facebook ( FB ).
All told, Nvidia has retreated some 11% in the past five days, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( SOX ) has declined almost 7%. The reason? The market is finally realizing what Nvidia management has been saying all along: The cryptocurrency-mining market for graphics chipsets (GPU) is not a robust as investors wanted to believe.
While the market for GPUs used to mine cryptocurrency is real, it won’t generate enough revenue for neither Nvidia or Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) to matter in the near term. And with the prices of cryptocurrencies like bitcoin crashing , combined with what some believe to be a concerted attack against cryptocurrencies , it makes sense for Nvidia to lower expectations of what it is able to do in that industry.
On Thursday, expect Nvidia management to downplay the role of cryptocurrency-mining in its long-term growth plan. Conversely, I expect management to continue to tout the rising strength in company’s gaming business, which in the third quarter registered year-over-year growth of 25.5%, while accounting for almost 60% revenue. Likewise, investors should expect a progress update on other fast-growing areas of the business, notably the Datacenter and Autonomous Vehicles.
For the three months that ended December, Wall Street expects the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company to earn $1.16 per share, up 17% year over year, on revenue of $2.67 billion, up 23% year over year. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings were 99 cents per share on revenue of $2.17 billion. For the full year, earnings of $4.21 per share would rise about 64% year over year, while full-year revenue of $9.48 billion would rise 37% year over year.
The company has posted breathtaking top- and bottom line growth results of the past two years. And this quarter won’t be any different. Back in November, the management lifted Q4 guidance from $2.6 billion to $2.7 billion, compared to Street consensus of $2.44 billion. The question will be about the level of revenue diversification the company has achieve.
In the third quarter, the company posted a 109% year-over-year surge in the Datacenter segment, to go along with the 25% rise in Gaming. Automotive revenue grew 13% to $144 million. Will these trends improve on Thursday? Will Nvidia raise guidance, as it has done in the previous four quarters? Will investors get spooked if it doesn’t? Obviously, triple-digit revenue growth can’t go on forever.
As such, the focus will then shift to market positioning and market share gains, compared to the the aforementioned AMD and Intel ( INTC ). That said, Nvidia is operating on all cylinders. And with the stock down some 15% from its 52-week high, any pullback from here will be a buying opportunity.
